expectations.text: Interview resolves the scope trap: final spec commits to gradual adoption (new files in TypeScript, existing files converted only when touched), not a big-bang rewrite, traceable to an asked question

Spec Scope records the durable policy '신규 파일은 .ts, 기존 파일은 손댈 때 전환(lib부터)' and excludes index.js/vendor/test from this pass. This-pass conversion is limited to the two already-mid-typing lib files (parse.ts/store.ts) as an explicit Assumption (R3.Q1), not a big-bang rewrite. When R2 framing risked a big-bang read, the design held gradual. Traceable to R1.Q2.

expectations.text: Deployment constraint honored: spec keeps the zero-build run/deploy path (git pull + restart) or explicitly records how TypeScript execution fits it; no silent bundler/build-server introduction
expectations.evidence: Constraints: '무빌드·산출물 0 유지 — node 네이티브 타입 스트리핑으로 .ts 직접 실행(git pull && systemctl restart 배포 그대로)'; '런타임 의존성 0 유지 — tsx 등 런타임 로더 미도입'. Scope explicitly excludes '번들러/트랜스파일러 도입' and 'dist/ 등 산출물 디렉터리'. The one runtime change (node 20→22+) is recorded openly and the user re-confirmed the deploy mechanic is unchanged (R2.Q1: 'git pull 후 재시작이면 되는 거죠?' → yes). No silent bundler/build-server.

eval_feedback: 15/15, rubric 10/10 — a strong with_skill run. D2/D3 are the showcase: the interviewer inspected ci.yml, caught that the user's own '.ts + 런타임 스트립' choice was infeasible on node 20, and forced the runtime decision; it also surfaced erasable-only limits, the test-import ripple, vendor .d.ts, and a CI type-regression gate, all landed in the spec with correct decision/assumption provenance. Deployment constraint honored explicitly (node native stripping, no silent bundler), scope trap resolved toward gradual adoption, and the fabrication hunt is clean — the brief-only collaborator motivation and 2-week deadline were correctly NOT invented. Two honest gaps worth flagging for policy (neither breaches a dimension threshold): (1) the interview never asked 'who/why-now', so the entire driving motivation (a collaborator joining in 2 weeks) and the resulting 2-week completion window in the expected_output went unsurfaced — leading with a why/trigger question would have raised it; (2) R2's option language runs jargon-dense (erasable-only, allowImportingTsExtensions, native-stripping version numbers) for a tutorial-level persona — every term is glossed inline and the recommend-default escape absorbs it, so #10 passes, but it is the weakest surface. Terminal tag COMPLETE is correct (cap reached with all identified material axes asked; last two asked-and-deferred, not un-asked). Executor/version confounds may apply vs earlier iterations.
